newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firmer, but off early highs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firmer, but off early highs.

text.p: Italian shares closed firmer on Tuesday but off early highs as Wall Street started lower this afternoon while volumes were generally light across many stocks.

Dealers said that stocks had recovered after Monday's losses which followed on from a surprisingly strong showing from the French political left in Sunday's elections, but lower U.S. stocks and the slow progress on welfare reform talks in Italy took the edge off prices during the afternoon.
The blue-chip Mib30 index of top Italian stocks ended up 0.67 percent at 18,371, while the all-share Mibtel closed 0.69 percent firmer at 12,237.

Dealers said that data today showing U.S. consumer confidence at a 28-year high in May put a break on Wall Street, but many in Italy were awaiting the government's three-year DPEF economic plan expected at the end of this week.
Reports Italian trade unions would have trouble accepting 8-9 trillion lire of cuts in pension and health spending in 1998 outlined in newspapers also kept stock investors cautious.

On individual stocks, Fiat was up 1.88 percent at 5,535 lire after chairman Cesare Romiti said in newspaper interview Monday the group's 1997 sales are seen around 90 trillion lire, while profits for the year will not be below 1996.

Among banking stocks, Banca Commerciale Italiana added 3.58 percent to 3,475 lire as talk it might take over Banca di Roma faded, while Credito Italiano rose 2.24 percent to 2,555 lire. San Paolo lost 1.07 percent to 10,680 lire after its public share offer closed on Friday.
Telecoms had a good showing with TIM up 0.75 percent at 5,133 lire, Telecom Italia 1.55 percent firmer at 4,707 lire and STET up 1.7 percent at 8,677 lire.
